heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
description: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Body Structure Strength
description: The body structure of all single deck buses of Type II and Type III category excluding Mini buses, shall be of sufficient strength, to meet the test requirements in Chapter 6, para 6.1.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Body Structure Stability
description: Stability Test of the body structure of single as well as double deck vehicles of categories Type I, Type II, Type III & Type IV shall meet the requirements test defined in Chapter 6, para 6.2.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Doors
description: The structure of the door shall be able to withstand distortion due to forces induced during its operation and the operability of door components critical to the removal of the passengers after an accident shall be ensured.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: The external side of the door shall not have any projection. The hinges and door handles shall meet requirements as specified in IS13942:1994, as amended from time to time
description: The external side of the door shall not have any projection. The hinges and door handles shall meet requirements as specified in IS13942:1994, as amended from time to time.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Door shall be fitted with weather resistant EPDM rubber seals of suitable design to avoid dust and water ingress
description: Door shall be fitted with weather resistant EPDM rubber seals of suitable design to avoid dust and water ingress.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Service doors
description: All Type I buses, except NDX shall be provided with Power Operated Service Door(s). The Power Operated Service Door shall be optional in the Type I NDX buses. Type II & Type III buses shall be provided with Power Operated or Manually Operated Service Doors(s).

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Service doors
description: Service door shall be capable of being easily opened from inside and from outside the vehicle when the vehicle is stationary. However this requirement does not preclude the possibility of locking the door from the outside, provided the door can be always opened from inside.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Service doors
description: The control or device for opening a service door from the outside shall be located at a height of 1000 mm to 1500 mm from the ground level. The measurement shall be carried out in the unladen condition on level surface

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Service doors
description: Single piece manually operated service door which is hinged or pivoted shall be such that in the event the open door comes in contact with a external object while the vehicle is in forward motion the door shall tend to close.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Service doors
description: Where direct view is not adequate, optical or other devices shall be installed to enable the driver to detect from his seat the presence of a passenger in the immediate interior or exterior vicinity of every service door.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Manually operated service doors fitted with slam type lock shall be of the two stage type
description: Manually operated service doors fitted with slam type lock shall be of the two stage type.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Service doors
description: On the inside of a service door there shall not be any device intended to cover the inside steps when the door is closed. The door operating mechanism and other equipment attached to the inside door should not pose safety hazard for the passengers.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Service doors
description: For every door which opens inwards, the mechanism shall be so constructed that its movement is not likely to cause injury to the passengers during normal use. Where necessary suitable protection devices may be provided.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Additional Requirements for Power Operated Service Doors
description: In the event of an emergency every power operated door shall be capable of - -being opened from inside when the vehicle is stationary even when locked from outside, by controls with or without power supply by which the door normally operates. - -Overriding all the other door controls. - -Being operated by a single person easily by hand. - -The controls shall be easily seen and identified by a person approaching the door or standing in Front of the door. - -The interior controls are placed on or within 300 mm of the door, at a height not less than 1,000 mm above the first step.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Additional Requirements for Power Operated Service Doors
description: The construction and control system of every power operated service door be such that a passenger is unlikely to be injured by the door or trapped between the door while closing. The door system shall meet the test requirements defined in Test methods para 6.5.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: The movement of the doors shall not be abrupt
description: The movement of the doors shall not be abrupt.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Activation of opening circuits
description: The opening controls of every automatically operated service door shall be capable of being activated and deactivated only by the driver from his seat. However provision in para 3.4.4.9.1 shall apply in the event of an emergency.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Activation of opening circuits
description: Activation of opening controls by the driver shall indicate the status by means of indicators (illuminated push button/sign) placed on or adjacent to the door whose control has been activated.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Opening of automatically operated Service Doors
description: After activation of the opening controls by the driver, the passenger shall be able to open the door by one of the methods below : - -from inside by a push button control or a passing through a light barrier. - -from outside by a illuminated push button clearly indicating status.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Closing of automatically operated Service Door
description: The automatically operated service door shall close automatically after a time interval of opening of the door. If a passenger enters or exits during this time interval, a safety device (e.g. a foot board contact, light barrier) shall ensure that the time until the door closes is sufficiently extended.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: If a passenger enters or exits while the door is closing, the closing process shall be interrupted and the door shall return to the open position
description: If a passenger enters or exits while the door is closing, the closing process shall be interrupted and the door shall return to the open position.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Emergency Doors
description: The emergency doors shall be capable of operation from both inside and outside when operated manually. However this requirement shall not be construed as precluding possibility of locking the door from outside provided the door can be opened from inside.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Emergency Doors
description: The outside handles of emergency doors shall lie within 200 mm on either side of centreline of the door drawn in the horizontal plane. However, the position of the outside handle shall not be more than 1800 mm above the ground level in the unladen condition.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Doors shall be hinged at the forward edge and in case of horizontal door the hinge shall be on the top edge
description: Doors shall be hinged at the forward edge and in case of horizontal door the hinge shall be on the top edge.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Emergency doors shall not be power operated or of sliding type
description: Emergency doors shall not be power operated or of sliding type.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Emergency doors shall open outward and shall be capable of remaining open outwards and at an angle of atleast 100 o , such that aperture is clear of any obstructions
description: Emergency doors shall open outward and shall be capable of remaining open outwards and at an angle of atleast 100 o , such that aperture is clear of any obstructions.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Door check, stay or strap which is capable of meeting requirements specified in para 3.4.5.1.5 may be used
description: Door check, stay or strap which is capable of meeting requirements specified in para 3.4.5.1.5 may be used.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: The forward edge of the emergency door shall be behind or in the same transverse plane tangent to the rear -most point of a seat back adjacent to it
description: The forward edge of the emergency door shall be behind or in the same transverse plane tangent to the rear -most point of a seat back adjacent to it.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Emergency Doors
description: All emergency doors shall be provided with an audible device to warn the driver when the emergency doors are not securely closed. The warning device shall operate due to the movement of the door catch and not by the movement of the door itself.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Emergency windows equipped with ejection type of construction shall be meet the requirement specified in IS 13944:1995
description: Emergency windows equipped with ejection type of construction shall be meet the requirement specified in IS 13944:1995.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Every hinged or executable emergency window shall open outwards
description: Every hinged or executable emergency window shall open outwards.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Every emergency window shall
description: Every emergency window shall:

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: either be capable of being easily and instantaneously operated from inside and from outside the vehicle by means of a device, or
description: either be capable of being easily and instantaneously operated from inside and from outside the vehicle by means of a device, or

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Every emergency window shall
description: be made of readily breakable safety glass. In such case a device shall be provided adjacent to each emergency window, available to the person in the vehicle for ready access for breaking the window. The window glass shall be made of safety glass as specified by Bureau of Indian Standards and shall readily break on impact when hit by a hammer in the event of an emergency.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Every emergency window which can be locked from outside shall be constructed such that it shall be capable of being opened at all times from inside
description: Every emergency window which can be locked from outside shall be constructed such that it shall be capable of being opened at all times from inside.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Emergency Windows
description: Emergency window where horizontally hinged at the top edge shall be provided with a suitable stay to hold the door fully open. Every emergency window shall operate such that it does not obstruct clear passage.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Every hinged emergency window which is not visible from the driver's seat shall be fitted with a audible warning device to warn failure of locking system
description: Every hinged emergency window which is not visible from the driver's seat shall be fitted with a audible warning device to warn failure of locking system.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Escape Hatches
description: Escape hatches shall be ejectable, hinged or readily breakable safety glass. Operation of escape hatch shall not obstruct clear passage from inside or outside the vehicle. Ejectable type hatches shall not detach from the vehicle fully.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Escape Hatches
description: Escape hatches shall be capable of being easily operated from inside and from outside the vehicle. However this requirement shall not be construed as precluding the possibility of locking the escape hatch for the purpose of securing the vehicle when unattended, provided that the escape hatch can always be opened from inside the vehicle.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: In case breakable safety glass is provided, a device shall be provided for breaking the escape hatch
description: In case breakable safety glass is provided, a device shall be provided for breaking the escape hatch.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Marking of Emergency Exits
description: All emergency exits shall be prominently designated in red letters in English when viewed from inside. Concise operating instructions describing each motion necessary to unlatch and open the exit shall be displayed. These instructions shall be located within 150 mm of the release mechanism. and by symbols when viewed from inside. Concise operating instructions describing each motion necessary to unlatch and open the exit shall be displayed. These instructions shall be located within 150 mm of the release mechanism.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Safety Signs - General Requirements
description: Each safety sign required by this Standard shall be used to communicate only one safety message. The information provided shall be in the form of pictograms, however, words, letters and numbers may supplement the pictogram in combination on the same sign. It shall be located and orientated so as to be easily understood.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Pictograms indicating a required action by the user shall show a person, or the relevant part of a person, operating the equipment or control device
description: Pictograms indicating a required action by the user shall show a person, or the relevant part of a person, operating the equipment or control device.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Safety Signs - General Requirements
description: Pictograms indicating a required movement shall, where appropriate, show an arrow pointing in the direction of motion. Where a rotational movement is required, a curved arrow shall be used. Safety signs shall follow the principles shown in the example layouts below;

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Where devices are to be operated, panels removed or doors opened, the pictogram shall indicate the action in progress
description: Where devices are to be operated, panels removed or doors opened, the pictogram shall indicate the action in progress.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: The lower case letter(s) of supplementary words, single letters and numbers shall have a minimum height of 10 mm
description: The lower case letter(s) of supplementary words, single letters and numbers shall have a minimum height of 10 mm.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: All safety signs shall be of photo-luminescent material
description: All safety signs shall be of photo-luminescent material.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: All safety signs shall comprise a Red pictogram on a White colour background
description: All safety signs shall comprise a Red pictogram on a White colour background.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Safety Signs - General Requirements
description: Safety signs identifying the control or the device for breaking/opening emergency windows/doors shall be positioned adjacent to, or surround all internal and external emergency controls for all exits.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Safety Signs - General Requirements
description: Safety signs shall not be located in positions where they may be obscured during operation of the vehicle. However, a curtain or blind may be positioned over an emergency window provided an additional safety sign indicates that the emergency window is located behind the curtain or blind.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Technical requirements for Retractable/Collapsible steps (if fitted)
description: Retractable/Collapsible steps if fitted shall comply with the following requirements:

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: The operation of Retractable/ Collapsible steps may be synchronized with that of the corresponding service or emergency door;
description: The operation of Retractable/ Collapsible steps may be synchronized with that of the corresponding service or emergency door;

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Technical requirements for Retractable/Collapsible steps (if fitted)
description: When the door is closed no part of the Retractable step shall project more than 10 mm beyond the adjacent line of the body work. Similarly, the collapsible step in non-usage position shall not intrude into passenger seat space or obstruct the emergency door access by more than 10mm.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Technical requirements for Retractable/Collapsible steps (if fitted)
description: When the door is open and the Retractable/Collapsible steps is in the extended position, the steps shall conform to the requirements of paragraph 2.2.5 of this standard;

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Technical requirements for Retractable/Collapsible steps (if fitted)
description: In the case of a manually operated step, when the step is in the extended position, an audible indication shall alert the driver when the step is not fully retracted or the emergency door is open.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Technical requirements for Retractable/Collapsible steps (if fitted)
description: If the device to operate the step fails, the step shall remain in the retracted position/original position. However, the operation of the corresponding door shall not be hindered in the event of such a failure or by the step being damaged or obstructed.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Technical requirements for Retractable/Collapsible steps (if fitted)
description: The corners of Retractable/Collapsible steps facing forwards or rearwards shall be rounded to a radius of not less than 5 mm; the edges shall be rounded to a radius of not less than 2.5 mm;

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Technical requirements for Retractable/Collapsible steps (if fitted)
description: When the passenger/emergency door is open, the Retractable/Collapsible step shall be securely held in the extended position. When a mass of 136 kg is placed in the centre of a single step or a mass of 272 kg is placed in the centre of a double step the deflection at any point on the step, measured relative to the body of vehicle, shall not exceed 50 - 60 mm.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Door components shall meet the requirements specified in Rule 124 of CMVR. The door components shall be meet requirements specified in para 6.6
description: Door components shall meet the requirements specified in Rule 124 of CMVR. The door components shall be meet requirements specified in para 6.6. Automotive Vehicles:- locking systems and door retention components - general requirement, Table 1 Standards Related to Door Components.Standard No = IS 14225-1995*. Automotive Vehicles:-window retention and release systems for buses, Table 1 Standards Related to Door Components.Standard No = 13944-1994*. * As amended from time to time, Table 1 Standards Related to Door Components.Standard No = * As amended from time to time

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Where windows with glazing are provided the glazing shall meet requirement specified as in para 3.6.2 & 3.6.3
description: Where windows with glazing are provided the glazing shall meet requirement specified as in para 3.6.2 & 3.6.3.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: The window glass shall be made of safety glass as specified in IS 2553 Part 2 and shall readily break on impact when hit by a hammer in the event of an accident
description: The window glass shall be made of safety glass as specified in IS 2553 Part 2 and shall readily break on impact when hit by a hammer in the event of an accident.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Minimum glazing thickness for windows, shall be as per IS:2553 (Part-2) as amended from time to time
description: Minimum glazing thickness for windows, shall be as per IS:2553 (Part-2) as amended from time to time.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Edges
description: The edge shall be crown edge, satin finish for all the exposed edges that is likely to come in touch with the passenger's body. (This Edge specification corresponds to Edge No. 1 specified in SAE J673).

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Window Frames
description: The glazing may be mounted on frame; constructed from aluminum extrusions or formed steel/coated sections. Alternately directly, sliding on flocked rubber channels supported by aluminum/steel section.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Window Frames
description: The window frames shall be mounted such that distortions and change of aperture dimensions due to forces on the structure does not deform the guideways. The window glass/glass and frame shall slide smoothly when subjected to normal pull force (50 to 75N)

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: The window frame shall be attached to the structure by weather strips or bonded with adhesive or any other suitable method
description: The window frame shall be attached to the structure by weather strips or bonded with adhesive or any other suitable method.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Window Frames
description: The mounting shall meet requirement specified in BIS Standard- Window retention and release system for Buses Safety Requirement IS 13944-1994. However, this requirement shall not be applicable for Mini buses whose Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is less than 3.5 tons.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Window Frames
description: The window frame fitted on buses shall meet the requirements specified in AIS-068 as amended from time to time however AIS-068 shall not be applicable for pasted or fixed glass windows Safety Glasses: Part 2 for Road transport, Table 2 Related standards for Window Glazing.Standard No = IS 2553 Part 2*. Window retention and release system for Buses:- Safety Requirement, Table 2 Related standards for Window Glazing.Standard No = IS: 13944-1994*. Water Proofing Test on Automobiles, Table 2 Related standards for Window Glazing.Standard No = IS 11865-1992*. * As amended from time to time, Table 2 Related standards for Window Glazing.Standard No = * As amended from time to time

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Ingress of dust and rain water
description: All body joints, front safety glass, rear safety glass, doors, windows and hatches should be so constructed such that it does not permit ingress of rain water, in the fully closed condition. It is recommended that the bus body builders carry out their own internal assessment test to check water proofing as per IS : 11865 - 1992.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Ingress of dust and rain water
description: All body joints, front safety glass, rear safety glass, doors, windows and hatches should be so constructed such that it does not permit ingress of dust, in the fully closed condition. It is recommended that the bus body builders carry out their own internal assessment test to check dust ingress as per IS : 11739 - 1986 as amended from time to time.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Drain holes shall be provided in the window frame such that water shall flow outward and does not flow into the structure cavity or into the passenger compartment
description: Drain holes shall be provided in the window frame such that water shall flow outward and does not flow into the structure cavity or into the passenger compartment.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Body Insulation
description: Body insulation shall be provided with suitable material for DLX and ACX buses and optional for other categories. It is recommended to use materials like Polyurethane or Glass Wool of minimum thickness of 40 mm and minimum density of 40 kg/m 3 . Materials superior to the ones shall also be permitted.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: The rear view mirrors shall meet the requirements specified in AIS Standards AIS-001 and AIS-002 as amended from time to time
description: The rear view mirrors shall meet the requirements specified in AIS Standards AIS-001 and AIS-002 as amended from time to time.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: The Wind Screen Wiping System shall meet the requirements specified in IS-15802:2008 as amended from time to time
description: The Wind Screen Wiping System shall meet the requirements specified in IS-15802:2008 as amended from time to time.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Vehicle Seats and Seat Belts
description: Vehicle Seats and Seat Belts

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: All Seat designs and Seat anchorage designs used in buses, shall meet the requirements of AIS-023 as amended from time to time
description: All Seat designs and Seat anchorage designs used in buses, shall meet the requirements of AIS-023 as amended from time to time.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Vehicle Seats and Seat Belts
description: All types of buses shall be provided with seat belts as per the provisions of CMVR. The seat belts assemblies and their anchorages shall meet the requirements of AIS-005 and AIS-015 as and when notified separately under CMVR.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: The Seats used in buses shall be those which are type approved by the testing agency as per AIS-023, as amended from time to time
description: The Seats used in buses shall be those which are type approved by the testing agency as per AIS-023, as amended from time to time.

subheading: Corrosion Protection
description: The quality of the surface treatment shall be tested according to the test methods specified in JIS D0202 or any equivalent standards including BIS Standard. (General Rules of Coating Films for Automotive Parts or equivalent Indian Standards using test panels.) The minimum quality requirements in table below shall be met for test criteria specified in para. 4 of JIS D0202. The compliance to this requirement shall be demonstrated by the body builder to the testing agencies. Oil Resistance (40 Deg. 24 hrs)h, Quality = No swelling, flaking, peeling, cracking, film softening nor appreciable change in lustre or colour. Volatile Oil Resistance (Gasoline) (24 hrs), Quality = No swelling, flaking, peeling, cracking, film softening nor appreciable change in lustre or colour. heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Engine Compartment
description: No flammable sound proofing material or material liable to impregnated with fuel, lubricant or any combustible material shall be used in the engine compartment unless the material is clad by an impermeable sheet.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Engine Compartment
description: Precaution shall be taken, either by suitable layout of the engine compartment or by provision of drainage orifices to avoid as far as possible, the accumulation of fuel, lubricants or any other combustible material in any part of the engine compartment.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Engine Compartment
description: A partition of heat-resistant material shall be fitted between the engine compartment and any other source of heat (e.g. a retarder designed to absorb energy liberated when descending along gradient). Any device designed for employing warm water shall be precluded from this requirement. All mounting clips gaskets etc. used in conjunction along with the device shall be fire resistant.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Fuel filler apertures shall be accessible only from exterior of the vehicle

subheading: Fuel feed System
description: Alterations shall not be permitted on fuel feed system provided by the vehicle manufacturer. The Coach builder shall obtain Type approval for carrying out any modification prior to any alteration if deemed necessary.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: No apparatus used for the fuel feed shall be placed in the driver's compartment or the passenger compartment
description: No apparatus used for the fuel feed shall be placed in the driver's compartment or the passenger compartment.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Fuel lines and all other parts of the fuel feed shall be accommodated in the vehicle where they have the optimum protection
description: Fuel lines and all other parts of the fuel feed shall be accommodated in the vehicle where they have the optimum protection.

heading: Standardization of the floor level height, gangways and dimensions of the foot steps
subheading: Fuel feed System
description: It is recommended that twisting and bending movements and vibrations of the vehicle or the power unit do not subject the fuel lines to abnormal stress. It is also recommended that the union of pliable pipes with rigid parts of fuel feed system must be so designed and constructed as to remain leak proof in various condition of use of the vehicle despite ageing, twisting or bending movements, or vibration of the vehicle structure or power unit. Fuel leaking from any part of the engine system be able to flow away freely to the road surface, but never into the exhaust system.

heading: Dimension of seats, seating layout, lighting and illumination
subheading: Driver Cabin lighting
description: The lighting devices used for cabin interior should be sufficient enough for clearly distinguishing each component part of the cabin. The driver should be in a position to read signages written on the walls, door of the cabin. He should also be in position to read any instructions printed on paper.

heading: Dimension of seats, seating layout, lighting and illumination
subheading: Driver Cabin lighting
description: The luminous flux of all the lamps provided for cabin lighting to light up the equipment, components and to read, shall not be less than 30 lux and shall not be more than 150 lux, when measured at 500 mm above the driver seat base.

heading: Dimension of seats, seating layout, lighting and illumination
subheading: The driver's compartment shall be provided with illumination through separate circuit
description: The driver's compartment shall be provided with illumination through separate circuit.

subheading: The following lamps fall in this category:- - -Exit lamps - -Passenger area lamps
description: The following lamps fall in this category:- - -Exit lamps - -Passenger area lamps

heading: Dimension of seats, seating layout, lighting and illumination
subheading: Passenger Compartment lighting
description: The lighting devices used for passenger area should ensure reading of signages inside the passenger area and other important signs like emergency signs. The illumination should light up handles, latches, knobs, rods, hand-holds, etc facilitating easy access to passenger. The illumination should be adequate for reading printed matter by the passenger.

heading: Dimension of seats, seating layout, lighting and illumination
subheading: The illumination of these lamps shall not be less than 50 lux, when measured at any seating location of the bus and at 500 mm above the seat base
description: The illumination of these lamps shall not be less than 50 lux, when measured at any seating location of the bus and at 500 mm above the seat base.

heading: Dimension of seats, seating layout, lighting and illumination
subheading: Passenger Compartment lighting
description: At least two night lights shall be provided in the passenger compartment of all buses except Type I buses. The interior lighting shall be designed such that the glare and reflections caused does not affect the driver.'

subheading: Luggage hold area lighting : Every luggage hold shall be provided with light fittings for illuminating the hold when in use
description: Luggage hold area lighting : Every luggage hold shall be provided with light fittings for illuminating the hold when in use.

heading: Dimension of seats, seating layout, lighting and illumination
subheading: Other Area Lightings
description: Destination panel lighting: The front, rear and side (optional) of the vehicle shall be illuminated or self illuminated (e.g. LED based destination boards) in such a way that the inscription on the panel/board shall be visible at a distance of 30 metres.

subheading: Other Area Lightings
description: Side marker lamp: These are to be mounted on the side of the vehicle and shall be of amber colour. They shall be mounted on a height of 250 - 1500 mm above the ground.

heading: Driver's workplace requirements
subheading: All cables used shall be compliant with BIS / DIN / ISO / SAE / JIS or JASO or other equivalent standard and shall be able to withstand working temperature upto 70°C
description: All cables used shall be compliant with BIS / DIN / ISO / SAE / JIS or JASO or other equivalent standard and shall be able to withstand working temperature upto 70°C.

heading: Driver's workplace requirements
subheading: Electrical cables
description: All the cables shall be ducted and secured at suitable places in such a manner that during normal use of vehicle the cables are not subjected to any tension, stretching, nicking, cutting, abrasion or chaffing.

heading: Driver's workplace requirements
subheading: The conductor cross section shall be selected to carry the rated current as given below or according to one of the standards mentioned in para 5.1.1
description: The conductor cross section shall be selected to carry the rated current as given below or according to one of the standards mentioned in para 5.1.1:-

heading: Driver's workplace requirements
subheading: Fuse
description: 1 = Every electrical circuit shall be provided with fuse designed for the circuit. In case of multiple circuits a common fuse shall be permitted, subjected to suitable current capacity per circuit depending upon the individual electric load.. 5.3, 1 = Terminals, Connectors & Elements. 5.3.1, 1 = End terminations: All the ends shall be suitably crimped with lugs /soldered or fixed so as to withstand vehicle vibrations.. 5.3.2, 1 = The interconnection shall be through couplers/junction boxes/ terminal blocks.. 5.3.3, 1 = Suitable connectors shall be used for external areas which are exposed to atmosphere to avoid water /moisture ingress during use.. 5.4, 1 = Safety requirements. 5.4.1, 1 = Use of relays and other electrical elements shall be adopted where the current rating of the switches is not adequate.. 5.4.2, 1 = The additional circuits shall not draw current more than specified by the manufacturer.. 5.4.3, 1 = Where the voltage exceeds 100 Volts RMS (Root Mean Square) in one or more electrical circuit, a manually operated isolation switch which is capable of disconnecting the circuit(s) from the main electrical supply shall be provided and shall be located inside the vehicle. Alternatively, electrically operated battery cut off switch may be provided.'. 5.4.4, 1 = No circuit provided by the vehicle manufacturer or type approved shall be modified.. 5.4.5, 1 = The isolation circuit shall have provision for bypassing circuits supplying mandatory external vehicle lighting i.e. besides the main isolation switch, individual isolation switches shall be used in series with main isolation switch, each for internal lighting and external mandatory lighting.. 5.4.6, 1 = Electrical cables shall be located such that no part can make contact with any fuel line or exhaust system subjected to excess heat. Suitable special insulation shall be provided where such electrical circuits are necessary.. 5.4.7, 1 = Electrical conductors shall meet the requirement for flame resistance specified in para 6.8.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
description: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers. 6. 2.2.18.4 Formula for calculation of seating and standee passenger areas - Area of the Driver Compartment, Description = Width x Depth of Driver Work Area. Area of the Driver Compartment, Area (in mm 2 ) = Ad. Total projected Step Well Area (all stepwells), Description = Sum of projected Area of all Step Wells. Total projected Step Well Area (all stepwells), Area (in mm 2 ) = As. Projected area of Engine, Description = Width x Length of Engine projected on the floor Area. Projected area of Engine, Area (in mm 2 ) = Ae. Area of any part of the Vehicle where vertical clearance is less than 1350 mm (Engine etc.), Description = -. Area of any part of the Vehicle where vertical clearance is less than 1350 mm (Engine etc.), Area (in mm 2 ) = Aw. Area required to provide a clear work area at service floor area occupied by any stair case, Description = -. Area required to provide a clear work area at service floor area occupied by any stair case, Area (in mm 2 ) = Ast. Area of parts where clear height above floor level less than 1900 mm (1750mm in case of mini bus), Description = -. Area of parts where clear height above floor level less than 1900 mm (1750mm in case of mini bus), Area (in mm 2 ) = Ac. Area of seat in facing partition, Description = ( 300 mm x Total seat width). Area of seat in facing partition, Area (in mm 2 ) = Ap. Area of the parts where slope exceeds the maximum specified value for purpose of passengers, Description = -. Area of the parts where slope exceeds the maximum specified value for purpose of passengers, Area (in mm 2 ) = Asl Total Area excluded for purpose of calculating seated passenger capacity, 1 = Sum (Ad+As+Ae+Aw+Ag+Ast+Ap). Total Area excluded for purpose of calculating seated passenger capacity, 2 = Aex. Area of Gangway, 1 = -. Area of Gangway, 2 = Ag. Total internal Floor Area, 1 = Internal Width x Internal Length. Total internal Floor Area, 2 = Aint. Area for seated Passengers, 1 = Aint-Aex. Area for seated Passengers, 2 = Apass. Area for standee passengers, 1 = Ag - (Ac + Asl + 150mm x Length of Gangway). Area for standee passengers, 2 = Astd Note : Value of Astd is the solution of following three equations - Aex = Ad + As + Ae + Aw + Asl + Ag + Ast + Ap Apass = Aint - (Aex + Ag) Astd = Aint - (Ad + As + Ae + Aw + Ast + Ac + Ap + Asl + Apass + 150mm x Length of Gangway)

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Design of Bus Bodies
description: All bus body builders may adopt suitable tools to design bus bodies for sufficient strength and for all the performance parameters specified in the code. Bus Body Builders may have their own analysis of bus body structures, done by use of Finite Element Analysis (FEA) or any other analytical tool to ensure sufficient bus body strength , for specific compliance to the strength requirements given at Clause 6.1. FEA is a detail design tool which basically saves time in designing and produces more accurate results. It is therefore recommended that bus body builders use design tools such as FEA, for verifying the strength of the bus body superstructure, either by themselves or from the authorised test agencies notified under Rule 126 of CMV(A)R, 1989. FEA would greatly help in assessing physical compliance to 6.1 at the design stage itself.

All Double Deck Buses of Type-II and Type-III category shall meet the requirements of body structure strength as per AIS: 031, as and when the body structure strength requirements are finalized and incorporated in AIS-031.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Test Condition
description: For the purpose of test the vehicle, the unladen vehicle with addition of : Load equal to 75 kg (68 kgs standard mass of passenger + 7kgs luggage) shall be placed on each passenger and crew seat. Where vehicle is designed to carry standee passengers a load of 75 Kg. is placed with its centre of gravity at a height of 875 mm from the floor. The load shall be uniformly distributed.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Test Condition
description: Alternatively a calculation method may be used to prove that the vehicle will not overturn under conditions specified in para 6.2.2.1.1. The Calculation method shall be approved by the test agency. The coach builder shall establish the validity of the calculation method to the satisfaction of the Test Agency on the basis of comparative test with a similar vehicle.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Test Method
description: The vehicle shall be subjected to test on a tilt test rig. Height of step used to prevent the vehicle from slipping side ways on the test rig shall not be greater than two third of the distance between the surface on which the vehicle stands and part of the rim of the wheel which is nearest to the surface in the untilted position. Ref. Fig. 8.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Test Requirements
description: The construction and control system of every power operated service door be such that a passenger is unlikely to be injured by the door or trapped between the door while closing. The door system shall meet the requirements defined in para 6.5.1.2 & para 6.5.1.3.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Test Requirements
description: The closing of the door at the measuring point is resisted by the clamping force not exceeding 150 N, the door shall reopen automatically to its fullest extent and remain open until a closing control is operated. The clamping force shall be measured using a test bar of section 60mm High 30mm Wide and rounded at corners (R=5mm). The clamping force may be measured by the method specified in 6.5.2 or by any other equivalent method specified by the test agency. The peak clamping force may be higher than 150 N momentarily provided that it does not exceed 300 N. Alternatively, if the door can be easily reopened by hand, if the clamping force measured does not exceed 80 N when the door is between 30 and 120 mm ajar, and 150 N when is between 120 mm and 400 mm ajar with the energy supply on.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Test Requirements
description: Whenever the doors are closed onto an object; the door reopens automatically to its fullest extent and remain open until a closing control is operated or the wrist or finger can be extracted without risk or injury to the passenger using test bar specified below: - -Test bar shall be so constructed such that it shall be tapered at one end over a length of 300 mm from 30 mm to a thickness of 5 mm.

subheading: Guidelines for measuring the closing forces of Power operated Doors
description: The closing of power -operated door is a dynamic process. When a moving door hits an obstacle, the result is a dynamic reaction force, the history of which (in time) depends on several factors. (e.g. the mass of the door, acceleration, dimensions ).

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Closing force F(t) is a time function, measured at the closing edges of the door (see para 6.5.2.3.2)

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Conditions of measurement
description: Conditions of measurement

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Temperature range 10  - 30  C
description: Temperature range 10  - 30  C.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: The vehicle shall stay on a horizontal surface
description: The vehicle shall stay on a horizontal surface.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Measurement Points Shall be: - -At the main closing edge of the door, - -one in the middle of the door; - -one 150 mm above the lower edge of the door;
description: Measurement Points Shall be: - -At the main closing edge of the door, - -one in the middle of the door; - -one 150 mm above the lower edge of the door;

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Measurement Points Shall be: - -At the main closing edge of the door, - -one in the middle of the door; - -one 150 mm above the lower edge of the door;
description: In case of the doors equipped with clamping prevention devices for the opening process; all the secondary closing edges of the door at the point which is considered to the most dangerous place of clamping.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: At least three measurements shall be taken at each of the measuring points to determine the clamping force according to para 6.5.2.2.5
description: At least three measurements shall be taken at each of the measuring points to determine the clamping force according to para 6.5.2.2.5.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Measurements
description: The signal of the closing force shall be recorded by means of a low- pass filter with limited frequency of 100 Hz. Both the threshold of sensitivity and fade away threshold to limit the pulse duration shall be set at 50 N.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: The deviation of the reading from the rated value shall not be more than  3%
description: The deviation of the reading from the rated value shall not be more than  3%.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Door Components
description: Door and door components shall meet the standard specified in Rule 124 of CMVR, door locks shall meet requirements laid out in BIS Standards, Automotive Vehicles : locking systems and door retention components general requirement IS 14225:1995, as amended from time to time and Automotive Vehicles Window retention and release system for buses safety requirement as specified in 13944-1995, as amended from time to time.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Door handle effort to unlatch the door shall be min. 30N and 55 N max. (optional specification)
description: Door handle effort to unlatch the door shall be min. 30N and 55 N max. (optional specification).

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Door latch
description: Longitudinal Load : The door latch and striker assembly when tested as defined in IS 14225:1995 shall withstand a ultimate longitudinal load of 11 KN, when in fully latched position and 4.45 KN when in secondary latched position.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Door latch
description: Transverse Load : The door latch and striker assembly when tested as defined in IS 14225:1995 shall withstand a ultimate transverse load of 8.9 KN, when in fully latched position and 4.45 KN when in secondary latched position.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Door latch
description: Inertia Load : The door latch when contained in the door latched system (door latch, striker assembly, outside handle, key cylinder and connecting mechanism) and in fully latched position must remain in fully latched position when subjected to inertia load of 30 g in any direction. (ECE -R-42 & SAE J 839 July 82)

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Door hinge must be capable of withstanding an ultimate longitudinal load of 1135 Kgf and Transverse load of 910 Kgf
description: Door hinge must be capable of withstanding an ultimate longitudinal load of 1135 Kgf and Transverse load of 910 Kgf.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Longitudinal Load : Door hinge system when subjected to test defined in SAE J July 82 shall be capable of withstanding an ultimate load of 11.1 KN
description: Longitudinal Load : Door hinge system when subjected to test defined in SAE J July 82 shall be capable of withstanding an ultimate load of 11.1 KN.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Transverse Load : Door hinge system when subjected to test defined in SAE J 934 July 82 shall be capable of withstanding an ultimate load of 8.9 KN
description: Transverse Load : Door hinge system when subjected to test defined in SAE J 934 July 82 shall be capable of withstanding an ultimate load of 8.9 KN.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Principle
description: This test consists of submitting specified test pieces of the electrical conductors, as installed in the vehicle, to a flame in order to evaluate their resistance to fire.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: The test equipment consists of
description: The test equipment consists of:

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: The test enclosure consists of metallic screen with 3 faces: - -1200  25 mm height, - -399  25 mm width, - -450  25 mm depth
description: The test enclosure consists of metallic screen with 3 faces: - -1200  25 mm height, - -399  25 mm width, - -450  25 mm depth. The front face is open and the top and bottom is closed. The base not be metallic.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Heat Source
description: The heat source consists of a gas burner (Bunsen burner) of internal diameter between 9.5 mm and 10 mm. Its control is such that the length of the outer flame is approximately 125 mm and that of the inner flame approximately 40 mm.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Heat Source
description: The functioning of the burner is tested in the following manner: the base of the burner being horizontal, a naked copper wire of 0.71  0.025 mm in diameter and having a free length of at least 100mm is introduced horizontally in to the flame, at 50mmabove the top edge of the wire is situated above the far vertical edge of the burner (see Fig. 9) the time necessary to melt the wire shall not exceed 6 seconds, nor be less than 4 seconds.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: The test piece is formed by a piece of conductor 600mm  25mm long
description: The test piece is formed by a piece of conductor 600mm  25mm long.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Test Method
description: The test piece is held vertically and placed in the middle of the test enclosure such that its lower end is approximately 50 mm from the base of the enclosure. For the test, the base of the burner ,forms an angle of 45 deg. With the axis of the test piece. The distance between the burner and the test piece must be such that the inner flame just touches the centre line of the sample(see Fig. 10). The flame must be applied about 100 mm above the lower end of the test piece for a continuous period T ( seconds) given by the formula: <!-- formula-not-decoded --> Where M is the mass in grams of the test piece of conductor per length of 600 mm.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: The observed phenomena are recorded in the test report, notably: - -the duration of the combustion - the length of the chared section
description: The observed phenomena are recorded in the test report, notably: - -the duration of the combustion - the length of the chared section.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Based on the results obtained, the material will be classified as follows
description: Based on the results obtained, the material will be classified as follows: Category 1: Combustion is self- extinguished. The upper end of the test piece is intact. - Category 2: Combustion is self- extinguished. - The upper end of the test piece is charred or affected. Category 3: Combustion is not self- extinguished.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Only Category 1 conductors are permitted
description: Only Category 1 conductors are permitted.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Reserved
description: Reserved

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Method of Measurement
description: For measurements of illumination as per Para 4.1.2.4.1.2.3 and Para 4.1.2.4.1.3.3, a lux meter shall be employed. After switching on the individual lighting devices, in as installed condition, the lux meter shall be placed at the location specified in Para 4.1.2.4.1.2.3 and Para 4.1.2.4.1.3.3 and then the lux values shall be noted. These lux values shall fall within the prescribed limits.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Cabin Lighting
description: The illumination by lighting devices lighting up the cabin interior should be sufficient enough to clearly distinguishing each component part of the cabin. Driver should be in a position to read signages written on the walls, door of the cabin. He should also be in position to read any instructions printed on paper.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: The following lamps are to fall in this category: - -Cab lamp or courtesy lamp - -Locker lamp - -Electrical distribution lamp
description: The following lamps are to fall in this category: - -Cab lamp or courtesy lamp - -Locker lamp - -Electrical distribution lamp

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Cabin Lighting
description: The luminous flux of all the lamps provided for cabin lighting to light up the equipment, components and to read, shall not be less than 30 lux and shall not be more than 150 lux, when measured at 500 mm above the driver seat base.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Passenger area lighting
description: Figure 1 Residual Space after Lateral Intrusion

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Passenger area lighting
description: The illumination by lighting devices lighting up the passenger area should ensure reading of signages inside the passenger area and other important signs like emergency signs. The illumination should light up handles, latches, knobs, rods, hand-holds, etc., facilitating easy access to passenger.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: The following lamps are to fall in this category:- - -Entrance lamps - -Passenger area lamps
description: The following lamps are to fall in this category:- - -Entrance lamps - -Passenger area lamps

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Passenger area lighting
description: The illumination of these lamps to light up the entrance and exit for the passengers and in general to light up the passenger compartment shall not be less than 50 lux. Illumination in passenger compartment shall be measured at any seating location of the bus and at 500 mm above the seat base.

heading: Methodology for the calculation of the standing and seating capacity for the passengers
subheading: Test methods, procedures and requirements in respect of items not covered in this code shall be separately notified time to time
description: Test methods, procedures and requirements in respect of items not covered in this code shall be separately notified time to time.

heading: Provisions for the persons with disabilities
description: Provisions for the persons with disabilities.

heading: Provisions for the persons with disabilities
subheading: The Type Approval Procedure specified in this code is applicable to buses with a seating capacity of 13 passengers or above
description: The Type Approval Procedure specified in this code is applicable to buses with a seating capacity of 13 passengers or above.

heading: Provisions for the persons with disabilities
subheading: SCOPE
description: The requirements of this code also apply to the following vehicles except in respect of those provisions* which are not compatible with the intended use and function of these vehicles : - A. High Capacity Buses like - i. Double Decker Bus - ii. Articulated Bus - iii. Double Deck Articulated Bus - B Special Purpose Buses like - - i. Sleeper Coach - ii. School Bus - iii. Tourist Bus - iv. Prison vehicles - v. Vehicles specially designed for the carriage of injured or sick persons (Ambulances) - vi. Off road vehicles - vii. Vehicle Designed for use by Police, Security and Armed Forces * Provisions to be defined and notified separately.

heading: Provisions for the persons with disabilities
subheading: SCOPE
description: The system for approval of Prototype (Rule 126) and Conformity to production (Rule 126A) to comply with provisions with respect to the safety, strength and technical requirements specified in the Bus body building code shall be based on the standards notified from time to time.

heading: Provisions for the persons with disabilities
subheading: Procedure for Type Approval
description: Procedure for Type Approval

heading: Provisions for the persons with disabilities
subheading: Procedure for Type Approval
description: The Type Approval shall be applicable to the following provisions for which compliance is sought by the vehicle manufacturer or Bus Body Builder as the case may be. - (i) Complete Vehicle Type Approval (or) - (ii) Bus Body Type Approval as a separate unit (or) - (iii) Vehicle Type Approval fitted with the Bus Body which is already type approved - (iv) Prototype Type Approval of Vehicle and other aggregates / units

heading: Provisions for the persons with disabilities
subheading: Application for Type Approval
description: The application for type approval shall be submitted to the test agency by the Vehicle Manufacturer / Bus Body Builder , with the description of the vehicle type (s) or body type (s) or the vehicle type fitted with an already approved body. This application shall be accompanied by the following documents, as applicable to the provisions for which compliance is sought. - a) List of provisions for which compliance is sought /to be established. - b) All the relevant information specified in the format ' Information on Technical Specifications' to be submitted by Bus Body Builder given in Table 22 and 22A of AIS-007(Rev.5):2014. - c) Copies of certificates or test reports of compliance to various provisions, which may have already been obtained from other recognized Testing Agencies. - d) Copies of test reports for other models/variants, if any, which can be used for establishing compliance of the model to be type approved, with a note explaining the details. - e) Copy of certificate of incorporation of the manufacturer, if not already submitted. - f) Publications available.

heading: Provisions for the persons with disabilities
subheading: Application for Type Approval
description: In case of body builders, who have adopted any type tested designs provided by the chassis manufacturers, the body builder shall provide the necessary details and drawings of the chassis manufacturer, to the test agency for their consideration.

heading: Provisions for the persons with disabilities
subheading: Type Approval of safety components / sub-assemblies
description: In addition to the safety components notified under Rule 124 of CMVR, 1989, the Type Approval of passenger seats and seat mountings, window sub-assembly, power operated service door, door components, etc shall be obtained.

heading: Provisions for the persons with disabilities
subheading: Methods of Establishing Compliance
description: Depending upon the provision, the compliance can be established by either comparison of the values declared in the Technical Specifications with those in the provisions of CMVR, or checking the fitment of part(s) on the vehicle or by testing, as applicable. Applicability of rules, method of establishing the compliance and details of the test procedures shall be as specified in the bus body building code.

heading: Provisions for the persons with disabilities
subheading: Certificate of Compliance: (Type-approval)
description: After compliance is established for all the provisions, applicable to that model/variant(s), a Certificate of Compliance consolidating all applicable provisions shall be issued by the Testing Agency. The Brief Technical Specifications as declared by the manufacturer (Table 22 and 22A of AIS-007 (Rev. 5): 2014) shall be counter signed by the Testing Agency and shall be attached to the certificate of compliance.

heading: Provisions for the persons with disabilities
subheading: Conformity of Production
description: COP shall be carried out at least once in 12 months by any of the testing agencies notified under Rule 126 of CMVR, 1989 or any other agency authorised by the government. A minimum of one unit shall be subjected to COP.

heading: Provisions for the persons with disabilities
subheading: Accreditation of Bus Body Builders
description: Accreditation of Bus Body Builders

heading: Provisions for the persons with disabilities
subheading: Accreditation of Bus Body Builders
description: All bus body building units shall be accredited by agencies notified by the Government. The accredited bus body building units shall meet the type approval requirements specified in para 7.2.

heading: Stability and strength evaluations of the bus body structure, seat anchorages etc., including the roll over test for the full body
description: Stability and strength evaluations of the bus body structure, seat anchorages etc., including the roll over test for the full body. The development of this Code was possible because of the commendable support and contributions made by the members of the Sub-Committee from ASRTU, ARAI, SIAM, CIRT, ACMA, representatives of others under the chairmanship of Mr. A. S. Lakra, the then Director - Engineering, ASRTU under the valuable direction and guidance of Shri B. Bhanot, the then Chairman-CMVR-TSC. Further, the CMVR-Technical Standing Committee in its 21 st meeting held on June 07, 2007 at New Delhi, realized the need for revision of the Bus Code and requested Shri Shrikant R. Marathe, Chairman-AISC to hold a separate sub-committee meeting with the stake holders for appropriate revision of the code. The specific concerns raised by the Vehicle industry, State Transport Corporations, and other stake holders were addressed in the meeting. Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST), Metropolitan Transport Corporation (MTC), ARAI, CIRT, VRDE and SIAM participated in the discussions. The sub-committee discussed various issues raised by the stake holders, during the meeting held on July 30, 2007. Further, as desired by the Chairman CMVR-TSC, during the special meeting on the Bus Code on March 08, 2008, at MOSRT&H, AISC had a separate meeting on April 04, 2008 at ARAI, specifically to discuss comments offered by Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) and SIAM for concluding the recommendations. There have been considerable changes in the ECE Regulation over a period of 7 years and the same had been considered for this revision exercise. The separate ECE Regulation 36 and 52 which was basically for the large capacity buses and small capacity buses have been put together to form ECE Regulation 107, which is common for all buses and coaches. The changes proposed by the stakeholders were examined in light of the revised Regulation ECE R 107, with a view to bring in more clarity on certain issues and to take care of editorial correction. The Midi and Mini buses which were addressed separately in our Bus Code have also been rationalized. The changes have been duly incorporated in the code and has been released as AIS-052 (Revision-1) - Code of Practice for Bus Body Design and Approval. This revised Code had the formal vetting of the CMVR-Technical Standing Committee, during its 24 th meeting held on July 14, 2008. AISC and CMVR-TSC sincerely thank all the stake holders for their effective contribution in the exercise of formulation of this code and revision of the same, which was co-ordinated by ARAI. To this end, the erstwhile Ministry of Surface Transport (MOST) has constituted a permanent Automotive Industry Standards Committee (AISC) vide order No. RT-11028/11/97-MVL dated September 15, 1997. The Standards prepared by AISC will be approved by the permanent CMVR Technical Standing Committee (CTSC). After approval, the Automotive Research Association of India, (ARAI), Pune, being the Secretariat of the AIS Committee, has published this Standard. For better dissemination of this information ARAI may publish this document on their Web site.

heading: Clause 1.0, Scope
subheading: The definitions given in AIS-008 and AIS-009 and their amendments in force at the time of application for type approval shall apply to this standard
description: The definitions given in AIS-008 and AIS-009 and their amendments in force at the time of application for type approval shall apply to this standard.

heading: Clause 1.0, Scope
description: " Retro-reflection " means the reflection in which light is reflected in directions close to the direction from which it came. This property is maintained over wide variations of the illumination angle.

heading: Clause 1.0, Scope
description: " Retro-reflecting optical unit " means a combination of optical components producing retro-reflection.

heading: Clause 1.0, Scope
description: " Retro-reflecting device " (also called ' Retro reflector ') means an assembly ready for use and comprising one or more retro-reflecting optical units.

heading: Clause 1.0, Scope
description: " Angle of divergence " means the angle between the straight lines connecting the centre of reference to the centre of the receiver and to the centre of the source of illumination.

heading: Clause 1.0, Scope
description: " Illumination angle " means the angle between the axis of reference and the straight line connecting the centre of reference to the centre of the source of illumination.

heading: Clause 1.0, Scope
description: " Angle of rotation " means the angle through which the retro-reflecting device is rotated about its axis of reference starting from one given position.

heading: Clause 1.0, Scope
description: " Angular diameter of the retro-reflecting device " means the angle subtended by the greatest dimension of the visible area of the illuminating surface, either at the centre of the source of illumination or at the centre of the receiver.

heading: Clause 1.0, Scope
description: " Illumination of the retro-reflecting device " is the abbreviated expression used conventionally to designate the illumination measured in a plane perpendicular to the incident rays and passing through the centre of reference.

heading: Clause 1.0, Scope
description: " Coefficient of luminous intensity (CIL) " means the quotient of the luminous intensity reflected in the direction considered, divided by the illumination of the retro-reflecting device for given angles of illumination, divergence and rotation.

heading: Clause 1.0, Scope
subheading: The symbols and units used in this standard are given in Annex A to this standard
description: The symbols and units used in this standard are given in Annex A to this standard

heading: Clause 1.0, Scope
description: A type of " retro-reflecting device " is defined by the models and descriptive literature submitted with the application for approval. Retro-reflecting devices shall be considered as belonging to the same type if they have one or more "retro-reflecting optical units" which are identical with those of the standard model, or if not identical are symmetrical and suitable for mounting one on the left and one on the right side of the vehicle, and if their other parts differ from those of the standard model only in ways not affecting the properties to which this standard applies.

heading: Clause 1.0, Scope
subheading: Retro-reflecting devices are divided into three classes according to their photometric characteristics: Class IA or IB, Class IIIA or IIIB, and Class IVA
description: Retro-reflecting devices are divided into three classes according to their photometric characteristics: Class IA or IB, Class IIIA or IIIB, and Class IVA.

heading: Clause 1.0, Scope
description: Retro-reflecting devices of Class IB and IIIB are devices combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight according to H-1.1 of Annex H , and which are integrated into the body of a vehicle. Note: The definitions of the technical terms (excluding the ones in AIS-008 and AIS-009) are those adopted by the International Commission on Illumination (CIE).
